subtopic: Repurchase Limits and Pro Rata Allocation
source_evidence: If shareholder requests for repurchase exceed the amount of outstanding shares eligible for repurchase during a repurchase offer, repurchase is generally done on a pro rata basis.
question: What happens when shareholders request more shares to be repurchased than an interval fund’s repurchase limit allows?
answer: Repurchases are generally allocated on a pro rata basis, so shareholders may be able to sell back only part of the number of shares they requested. There is no guarantee that a shareholder can sell all the shares they requested in a given offer.
